title: Routing graceful degradation: fallback to compatible model variants on burn spikes (tier-aware guardrails)
author: Elena Popov
description: Motivation: We’ve been treating error budget burn primarily as an alerting signal, but we don’t consistently translate it into automated mitigation. When burn spikes (typically a combination of elevated 5xx/timeouts and/or latency), we can reduce blast radius by routing away from the degraded surface area (model, region, or route) to known-compatible fallbacks while keeping tier guarantees intact. This PR adds a routing-side graceful degradation policy keyed off burn signals, including explicit guardrails for Dedicated pools to preserve isolation and customer pinning expectations. What’s in this PR: (1) New “degradation controller” in smart routing that consumes burn status from control plane and emits a per-scope routing decision (prefer/avoid) for {tier, region, route, model_family}. (2) Fallback selection: for chat/completions we can route to a compatible variant (same family, compatible tokenizer + context length class, and explicitly allowed by catalog compatibility map). For embeddings, fallback is restricted to variants with matching embedding dimension + verified normalization behavior. (3) Tier-aware guardrails: Hosted can fallback across shared capacity (within region, then cross-region if enabled), but Dedicated is restricted to (a) within the same customer’s dedicated pool, (b) only to customer-approved variants, and (c) never cross-customer or cross-pool. If Dedicated pool is degraded and no approved fallback is available, we fail fast with a clear error + Retry-After rather than silently routing to Hosted. (4) Config + flags: feature flag routing.degrade_on_burn (default off), plus policy config for burn thresholds and max fallback aggressiveness. (5) Observability: new counters for degradation decisions, fallback hits/misses, and “blocked by guardrail” reasons (to make it obvious when we chose correctness over availability). Rollout plan: ship behind routing.degrade_on_burn, enable in canary for Hosted first (us-east-1 + eu-west-1, /v1/chat.completions streaming + non-streaming), then expand. Dedicated remains disabled by default; can be enabled per-customer after validating “approved variants” config and readiness of pool-level SLO dashboards. Notes: This is not a substitute for fixing underlying issues; it is an automated mitigation to buy time and prevent cascading failure while we burn budget. It also intentionally avoids using customer-perceived timeouts as burn input (those are excluded elsewhere); we only consume server-side burn computations. Links: Linear ENG-2423; related work: PR #18421 (budget-check endpoint), PR #18433 (tier propagation), Confluence error budget policy (draft).

conversation: Mina Haddad (review) — 2026-02-13: The overall approach makes sense. Two concerns: (1) Dedicated must never silently route to Hosted even if compatibility exists; (2) make sure we don’t create an oscillation where fallback increases load on the fallback model and causes it to burn too. Can we add a minimum hold time / hysteresis and a cap on fraction of traffic we’ll move? Elena Popov (author) — 2026-02-13: Agree on (1) — I’ve tightened the guardrail so Dedicated can only route within pool_id and only if the customer has allow_fallback=true and the target_model is in approved_variants. For (2), I added hysteresis (enter degrade after 2 consecutive polls above threshold; exit after 3 consecutive below) and a max_shift_pct config (default 20% per 5m window). Ravi Menon (review) — 2026-02-14: Compatibility map: can you confirm embeddings fallback is dimension-safe? We had an issue where downstream assumed 1536. Also, for chat variants, tokenizer compatibility isn’t enough; we should require a catalog-declared “serving_compatible_with” mapping. Elena Popov — 2026-02-14: Updated: embeddings fallback now requires exact embedding_dim match plus catalog flag embedding_normalization=cosine_unit (or exact match of normalization). For chat, fallback now uses catalog-declared serving_compatible_with, not heuristic tokenizer checks. Added tests and a log when compatibility is missing. Jordan Lee (review) — 2026-02-15: Policy wiring: we should prefer reading burn status via control plane but ensure the caller is tier-scoped (otherwise one tier’s burn could affect another). Also ensure the request context includes tier propagated from gateway. Elena Popov — 2026-02-15: Burn status fetch is now keyed by {tier, service=routing, region} plus optional model_family. Evaluator only applies decisions that match the request tier. Added a defensive check: if tier is missing in request context, we do NOT apply degradation (fail closed) and emit routing_degradation_tier_missing. Amara Diallo (review) — 2026-02-15: Retry-After header: please ensure we only set this for server-side 503s and not for auth/4xx; also align with gateway behavior. Elena Popov — 2026-02-15: Fixed: Retry-After is only set when guardrail blocks fallback and we return 503 with reason=dedicated_pool_degraded_no_fallback. No changes to 4xx paths. Aisha Bello (review) — 2026-02-16: From SRE POV: can you add a metric label for why fallback was blocked (e.g., not approved, cross-pool, cross-tier)? That’s critical when debugging Dedicated escalations. Elena Popov — 2026-02-16: Added routing_degradation_blocked_total{reason=...} with reasons: not_approved, cross_pool, cross_tier, no_compatible_variant, feature_flag_disabled. Mina Haddad — 2026-02-16: Looks good with the hysteresis + cap. Approving. Ravi Menon — 2026-02-16: Approve once the flake is fixed. Jordan Lee — 2026-02-16: Approved. Elena Popov — 2026-02-16: Pushed fix for flake (removed wall-clock dependency, uses fake clock). CI green now.
release_notes: Internal-only (behind feature flag): Adds tier-aware routing graceful degradation triggered by error budget burn spikes. Hosted can fallback to compatible model variants; Dedicated enforces pool isolation + customer-approved variants only.
outcome: Merged to main (squash). Feature flag routing.degrade_on_burn remains OFF by default; rollout via canary config change tracked in ENG-2423.
